description: Binding backup, PITR, object retention and isolated restore policy for Memory OS. Object versioning is not backup completion, backup creation is not restore proof, and a healthy restored service is not safe until deletion and expired-session non-resurrection are verified.
principles: backup creation and restore verification are separate evidence
object versioning is not an independent backup
recovery point and recovery time objectives must be explicitly approved before production
restores occur in an isolated environment with normal user traffic disabled
deleted accounts, memories, Previews, objects and expired or revoked sessions must not silently reappear
tenant isolation, FORCE RLS and authority boundaries are reverified after restore
database and object recovery points must be correlated or inconsistency must fail closed
backup credentials and restore authority are narrower and independently owned
backup evidence excludes secrets and unnecessary personal content
promotion of a restored environment is an incident-command decision, not an automatic health-check action

includes: exact object version IDs and authoritative metadata
objects retained for retry, deletion or incident evidence
parser adapter versions and artifact digests
append-only incident decisions and evidence references

requiredActions: create restore run or incident id
record reason, target time, source backups and owners
identify affected tenants and deletion/session risk
define promotion prohibition and verification plan
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: restore target, authority, evidence sources and safety constraints are explicit

requiredActions: identify PostgreSQL base backup and WAL/PITR target
identify matching or safely bounded object versions
record migration/release/parser generations
record expected data loss and object/database skew
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: selected recovery point is internally coherent or known inconsistency is classified fail-closed

requiredActions: restore into a network- and identity-isolated environment
disable normal user traffic, outbound side effects and production credentials
apply no destructive cleanup before evidence capture
record exact restore commands and results without secrets
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: restored environment is available only to the approved verification team

requiredActions: verify migration sequence and schema checksums
verify runtime roles, NOBYPASSRLS, NOINHERIT and FORCE RLS
run cross-tenant negative tests
verify parser artifact and object-version bindings
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: schema, authority and exact-version invariants pass independent verification

requiredActions: verify Preview candidate/rejection/accounting consistency
verify Apply confirmations and memory item accounting
verify exact idempotent replay behavior
verify database/object metadata coherence
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: restored canonical state is internally accounted and repeatable

requiredActions: verify deleted accounts remain fenced or deleted
verify deleted memories, Previews and objects do not reappear
verify expired and revoked sessions remain unusable
verify replay-protection and account-epoch semantics
record any intentionally retained backup-only data and its access restrictions
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: deletion and session non-resurrection checks pass or restore remains isolated

requiredActions: measure actual recoverable point against the incident target
measure elapsed restore and verification time
compare measured values to approved RPO and RTO
record backlog and catch-up behavior
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: RPO/RTO result is measured and classified without inventing a target

requiredActions: obtain incident commander, system owner and security/privacy approval
record residual data loss, skew and open risks
define cutover, rollback and user communication plan
keep promotion blocked when any critical verification is incomplete
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: promotion is explicitly approved or explicitly refused with evidence

requiredActions: preserve append-only restore evidence
record failed checks and remediation owners
update retention, monitoring and runbooks
schedule the next independent restore rehearsal
restoreLifecycle.exitCriteria: restore evidence is retained and all gaps have owners

tenantAndAuthority: runtime role remains NOBYPASSRLS and NOINHERIT
account epoch and authority boundaries hold
previewApply: idempotent replay returns the original result
sessionsAndReplay: authorization-code and nonce replay remains rejected
raw bearer tokens absent from evidence
deletion: deleted memory and Preview rows do not become user-visible
deleted or expired object versions follow the approved retention/deletion policy
deletion worker state does not repeat unsafe side effects
objectsAndParser: exact object key, version, length, checksum and metadata
required parser artifact digest is available
unknown artifact or persisted version fails closed

promotionGuards: restored environment has not passed cross-tenant negative tests
deleted data or expired/revoked session non-resurrection is unverified
database and object recovery points are inconsistent beyond an approved bound
required object version or parser artifact is missing
migration sequence or release compatibility is unknown
RPO or RTO target is undefined for a production promotion decision
restore used production credentials or emitted external side effects
incident commander, system owner or security/privacy approval is missing
critical verification result is FAIL, PARTIAL or NOT_RUN

requiredDrills.scenario: clean isolated restore of current PostgreSQL and correlated object state
point-in-time restore across an in-flight Preview and Apply boundary
restore after account deletion and session expiry/revocation
restore where database and object recovery points are intentionally skewed
restore while a required old parser artifact or object version is unavailable

readiness.note: Backup/restore policy, verification and promotion guards are defined. No production PostgreSQL backup/PITR, independent object retention, RPO/RTO, isolated restore environment or completed restore drill is claimed, so OPS-P0-007 remains PARTIAL_FOUNDATIONS_ONLY.
